text:
The Blues' story right now is in the crease. Joel Hofer has been on a heater: a .933 save rate over his last five starts, saving 5.3 more goals than an average goalie would on the same shots. Jordan Binnington has gone the other way, .843 and 3.7 goals worse than expected over his last five. Binnington has also had 15 headlines in two weeks, most of them trade speculation (Edmonton's name keeps coming up), so every Hofer start reads a little louder.

The team in front of them is a coin flip, and that's not an insult. St. Louis is 11-9-2 with 24 points, has scored and allowed exactly 67 goals, and holds 49.7% of the expected goals, the quality of chances. Our numbers say their record is almost exactly what their play has earned, and they're 6-3-1 in their last ten. Their playoff chances sit around 42%.

The Robert Thomas, Dylan Holloway and Jimmy Snuggerud line plays the most minutes and wins them narrowly; the Connor McMichael and Mason McTavish group creates the most. Justin Barron has 8 points in his last 10 games, well above the 4.1 his chances suggest, and Logan Mailloux is back after making his season debut off injured reserve on Nov. 10.

We'd watch two things: who starts the next big game, and whether the shooters, who've scored about four goals fewer than their chances deserve, start to catch up.
headline: Hofer's net, Binnington's rumours
